title: School Basketball Uniform Order Checklist: 12 Points for Athletic Directors
excerpt: A practical 12-point ordering checklist for athletic directors, coaches and school buyers covering roster planning, mixed sizing, artwork, samples, quality control, reorders and delivery.

children.text: Ordering school basketball uniforms involves more than selecting a jersey design. Athletic directors and coaches need to coordinate the roster, youth and adult sizes, player names and numbers, approval responsibilities, production timing, reorders and delivery. The safest approach is to approve one controlled order specification before bulk production begins.
Quick Answer

Before requesting a final quotation, prepare the school name, team level, quantity, roster, size mix, required delivery date, preferred uniform package, logo files, color references and personalization list. Before bulk production, approve the 3D mockup, physical sample, size specification and final roster. Before shipment, request a quality inspection covering artwork, colors, stitching, measurements, names, numbers, quantities and packaging.
1. Identify the Decision Makers

Confirm who can approve the design, pricing, sample and final production. School orders often involve a coach, athletic director, purchasing office and finance department. The manufacturer should receive one final approval from the authorized buyer rather than conflicting instructions from several contacts.
2. Set the Required Delivery Date

Start with the date the uniforms must arrive at the school, not the first game date. Allow time for internal approval, mockup revisions, sample review, bulk production, quality control and shipping. POXIOL's standard planning reference is Sample Production in 2–3 Days After Mockup Confirmation, bulk production usually takes 7–12 working days after sample or artwork approval; large, complex, or peak-season orders require a confirmed production schedule, and shipping in 3–7 Business Days Depending on Country.
3. Build One Controlled Roster

Use one spreadsheet containing player name, jersey number, top size, shorts size, team level and any special requirement. Assign one person to control the latest version. Do not send names, numbers and sizes across separate email or chat messages because this increases the risk of duplicate numbers, spelling errors and outdated sizes.
4. Confirm Youth and Adult Size Requirements

Schools may need youth and adult sizes in the same order. Confirm whether the manufacturer supports mixed sizing and request the exact finished-garment size chart. Use garment measurements rather than relying only on age labels. Record any approved size tolerance and identify unusually small, tall or broad players before production.
5. Define the Uniform Package

State exactly what every player receives. Common packages include jersey and shorts, reversible jersey and shorts, or a wider program including warm-up tops, hoodies, shooting shirts and coach apparel. Confirm whether socks, bags, labels and individual packaging are included or quoted separately.
6. Lock the Design and Personalization

Provide the school logo in a usable vector or high-resolution format and confirm that the school owns or is authorized to use all submitted artwork. Approve the front logo, back layout, player names, numbers, sponsor marks, collar style, side panels and color references. Avoid using protected league, professional team or third-party brand artwork without authorization.
7. Approve Fabric, Fit and Construction

Ask the supplier to confirm fabric composition, weight, stretch, breathability and intended use. Review collar and armhole construction, reinforced seams, waistband structure and print coverage. The correct option depends on whether the uniform is for regular school competition, intensive training, reversible use or a retail-style team program.
8. Review the Free 3D Mockup

The mockup should show front and back views, colors, logo placement, number style and the overall team identity. Check spelling and placement before approving it. A mockup confirms the visual direction but does not replace a physical sample review for fit, fabric and workmanship.
9. Approve a Physical Sample

Review the sample under normal lighting and, where possible, have a player test the fit. Check fabric hand feel, color accuracy, print sharpness, stitching, measurements, collar comfort, shorts waistband, logo position and player details. Record every approved change in writing before bulk production.
10. Freeze the Bulk Production File

Before production begins, approve one final file containing the artwork, roster, sizes, quantities, names, numbers, packaging instructions and delivery address. Mark older versions as superseded. Late changes should be accepted only after the manufacturer confirms whether production has already started.
11. Plan for Reorders

Schools often need replacement uniforms for new players, damaged garments or future seasons. Confirm whether the manufacturer stores the design record and can reproduce the same artwork later. Keep the approved design version, fabric reference, size chart and color information in the school's purchasing records.
12. Complete Pre-Shipment Quality Inspection

Before shipment, verify total quantity, size distribution, player names, numbers, artwork, color consistency, fabric, stitching, measurements and packaging. Request photos or inspection records where appropriate. POXIOL's standard workflow includes Pre-Shipment Quality Inspection before the order leaves the factory.
Information to Send With Your First Inquiry

Send the sport, school or team name, country, required delivery date, estimated quantity, youth and adult size requirements, uniform package, logo files, preferred colors, player personalization needs and shipping destination. Providing this information at the beginning allows the supplier to prepare a more accurate mockup, quotation and production plan.
Final Recommendation

The most reliable school basketball uniform order is based on one approved roster, one artwork version and one production specification. Do not approve bulk production until the mockup, physical sample, sizes, player details and delivery plan are confirmed. This process reduces avoidable corrections and creates a clear record for future reorders.

keyTakeaways: 1. Confirm the final roster, size mix and required delivery date before artwork approval.
2. Keep youth and adult sizing in one controlled roster sheet instead of sending sizes through separate messages.
3. Approve both the 3D mockup and a physical sample before bulk production.
4. Save the approved artwork, color references, names, numbers and size records for future reorders.
5. Complete a pre-shipment quality inspection before the uniforms leave the factory.
6. POXIOL supports MOQ 1 Set, a Free 3D Mockup and Sample Production in 2–3 Days After Mockup Confirmation.

title: How to Choose Fabric and GSM for Youth Basketball Uniforms
excerpt: GSM alone cannot determine whether a basketball uniform is suitable. Evaluate garment structure, climate, activity intensity, hand feel, breathability and sizing together, then confirm the available fabric through a traceable swatch or finished sample.

children.text: 30-Second Answer

GSM is a fabric mass-per-area measure, not a stand-alone quality, breathability, durability or comfort score. For a basketball uniform, combine fabric structure, single-layer or double-layer construction, climate, activity intensity, age and size, training frequency, care method and a representative physical sample before approving the specification.
What GSM Means

GSM is mass per area: it helps a buyer compare the mass of a particular fabric sample on a consistent area basis. It does not make two fabrics with the same number feel the same: yarn, knit or weave, mesh openings, finish, stretch and panel construction can change hand feel, ventilation and movement. Treat the number as one comparison input and ask for a traceable fabric reference or supplier record rather than inventing a measurement.
What GSM Does Not Mean
GSM alone cannot prove breathability, moisture-wicking or drying behavior.
It cannot prove abrasion life, stretch and recovery, colorfastness or softness.
It cannot predict the finished uniform weight because size, panels, trims, decoration and layers also matter.
It cannot establish suitability for every age group, body shape, activity intensity or climate.
Single-Layer, Double-Layer and Reversible Structure Changes the Wearing Experience
Single-layer uses one primary garment layer; review the fabric, fit and panel layout together.
Double-layer adds another material layer and construction decision, so compare hand feel, ventilation, opacity and movement on the finished sample.
Reversible construction is designed for two wearable visual sides and may change neck, sleeve, seam and care checks.
For training and games, confirm whether two-sided visual use is required and whether the sample works in the intended setting.
Construction, material use, personalization, packaging and review scope can affect cost; no structure is automatically better.
Approve the sample before bulk production because GSM alone cannot predict the complete wearing experience.
Use-Case Selection
For hot or humid conditions, prioritize a sample review of ventilation, hand feel, fit and movement in representative use.
For indoor training or games, compare the complete garment against the activity intensity and layering needs.
For high-frequency training, document rotation, wash routine and decoration care instead of assuming a fixed life.
Youth teams, schools and clubs should align the structure with roster control, season use and fitting evidence.
If training or competition needs two visual sides, inspect the reversible sample from both sides.
If a lightweight feel matters, compare traceable finished samples rather than treating a GSM threshold as a promise.
Age, Size and Fit
Youth and Adult sizing cannot be selected by GSM alone. Size, pattern, garment length, chest room and movement space affect comfort.
Use a representative sample on people in the target age range and near the intended size, then record fit observations.
For reversible garments, check the neckline, sleeve openings, inner and outer layers and the fit after turning the garment inside out.
Keep the approved size chart and finished measurements with the fabric reference so later reorders use the same decision record.
Training Frequency and Care
Record weekly use frequency and whether the roster needs a rotation of uniforms.
Confirm washing and drying methods for the approved fabric and decoration.
Ask how names, numbers, logos and other personalization should be maintained during care.
For repeat orders, confirm that the same traceable fabric and approved sample remain available; do not promise a fixed service life.
Verified Fabric and GSM Availability

Exact fabric names, measured GSM values and current supply status must come from a traceable swatch, measurement record or current supplier confirmation. Where that evidence is unavailable, POXIOL confirms the available reference during quotation and sampling rather than publishing an invented specification.
Sample Testing Checklist (Sample Test Checklist)
Fabric name or internal identification code.
Measured or supplier-confirmed GSM for the traceable reference.
Single-layer, double-layer or reversible construction.
Hand feel and skin-contact comfort.
Ventilation and movement during representative activity.
Stretch and recovery response.
Neckline, sleeve openings and seam construction.
Color and design reproduction against the approved artwork.
Name, number and logo placement.
Size, garment length and movement room.
Appearance after the agreed wash and dry routine.
Consistency with written specifications and the approved mockup.
If real test evidence is not available, record that the swatch or finished-garment sample still requires verification.
Quotation Information Checklist (Information to Send for a Quotation)
Product type.
Single-layer, double-layer or reversible structure.
Intended age group.
Size range and quantity.
Climate and use scenario.
Training or game frequency.
Logo, number, name and personalization requirements.
Target delivery.
Receiving country or postal code.
Label and packaging requirements.
Whether a sample should be made first.

children.text: Yes. POXIOL can customize player names, numbers, team logos, sponsor graphics and original pattern designs.

question: What products can POXIOL manufacture?

children.text: POXIOL can manufacture custom basketball uniforms, soccer kits, baseball uniforms, training wear, warm-up sets, team hoodies, jackets, accessories and private label teamwear collections.

question: Does POXIOL provide factory audit reports?

children.text: Yes. POXIOL maintains transparent manufacturing standards. We can provide factory inspection details, production capacity data, and QC checklists upon request for authorized B2B distributors and brand partners.

question: How fast can POXIOL make a sample?

children.text: For standard custom teamwear projects, sample production can usually be arranged in 2–3 days after mockup confirmation.

question: Can POXIOL make full soccer kits?

children.text: Yes. POXIOL can produce soccer jerseys, shorts, socks, goalkeeper kits and training wear.

question: What logo file format is required for high-precision sublimation?

children.text: B2B buyers should provide original vector files in .AI, .EPS, or .SVG formats. This allows our design team to scale logos for youth and adult sizes without any loss of sharpness or resolution.

question: Can POXIOL provide a free mockup?

children.text: Yes. Buyers can send sport category, logo, colors, quantity and reference design. POXIOL can prepare a free visual mockup before sampling or bulk production.

question: What happens after I submit a free mockup request?

children.text: POXIOL reviews your project details, prepares a visual mockup or sourcing recommendation, confirms sample requirements, and then provides a quotation and production plan.

question: Can POXIOL use official club or tournament logos?

children.text: No. POXIOL only supports buyer-owned, original or properly authorized artwork and does not provide unauthorized protected team crests, league marks or tournament logos.

question: What is the minimum sample order?

children.text: The draft procurement standard lists a minimum sample order of one set.

question: How long does sample production take?

children.text: Sample production normally takes 2-3 days after mockup confirmation.

question: How long does express delivery take?

children.text: Express delivery commonly takes 3-7 business days depending on destination and carrier.
